dataList.title: The Exemplar Fixer
dataList.eventDesc:
"Hey, hey. Look at this part over here."
"Point #3: Popping your collar will have an intimidating effect on your opponent."

The Fixer in the ill-fitting coat explained, tracing a line from the interview in the magazine with his fingertip.

"So I followed the advice right here... just like this."

"How's that? Feeling intimidated?"

... Where should we even begin? More importantly, who's going to tell him?
successDesc: "Uh, but here, it says..." {0} pointed out another phrase from the interview. "Two rules all excellent Fixers must abide by:" "First, don't be a copycat." "Second, follow the first rule no matter what." "......." "... Look, it's all about being original, see?" "I guess you have a point... I want to be like him, not actually be the same person..." The Fixer in the ill-fitting coat gravely contemplated the two rules for a moment, then rolled up the sleeves of the oversized coat. "Thanks. It seems that I've been neglecting what's really important all along." The two Fixers walked away, smiling like a weight had been lifted from their shoulders. "Wait, you forgot the mag—" The magazine was well-worn with pages upon pages of underlined and highlighted phrases, but it seemed that the young Fixer no longer had any need for it.
failureDesc:
{0} stared at the photo for a long, long time, then began.

"First, pop your collar some more..."

"Like this?"

"Ehh, I ain't seein' the vision. Maybe try rollin' up those sleeves."

"Are ya sure that's the problem here? Look, he's holding the weapon in his right hand."

"But I'm left-handed."

"Hm! Then I daresay 'tis an opportunity most wonderful to cultivate thy skill in the field of ambidextrousness!"

The young Fixer and the Sinners all came together to contemplate what to do, but no matter which direction we tackled it from, the discussion seemed to return to square one.

"So... I appreciate you trying to help, I really do, but... this really isn't working out, guys. I'll just try to figure it out on my own. Thanks for trying."

"Stubborn bastard, isn't he? ... Ah, I'm sorry. I've wasted your time for nothing."

... The Fixer in the ill-fitting coat walked away, his face buried in that magazine all the way.

dataList.title: Dawn Office
dataList.eventDesc:
There was no way we could be comfortable sitting around and sipping from teacups when we'd just barged into this guy's office without an explanation.
Besides, there were about a dozen of us, and the teapot was nowhere near large enough to hold enough tea for so many guests.
We gingerly suggested brewing our own batch of ssanghwa-cha.

"You want to brew your own batch...?"

The glasses-wearing Fixer looked back and forth between us and the teapot, then...

"I don't really mind doing it myself, but... sure. Give it a try."

... moved to the side, gesturing us toward the pot.
dataList.behaveDesc: Who will try brewing a cup of ssanghwa-cha?
successDesc:
We added the ingredients in the order explained to us by the young Fixer.
When the water came to a rolling boil, we reduced the heat, letting the ingredients simmer gently.
Our impromptu tea instructor opened his mouth a few times as if to interject, but he eventually settled into quiet observation.

With the batch of ssanghwa-cha completed, we poured it into a cup and carefully placed a bright yellow egg yolk on top.

"Ohh... I must say, this does look the part."

After that brief compliment, the old man took a sip of our ssanghwa-cha... and nodded, his lips drawn into a kindly smile.

"Are you sure this is the first batch you've ever brewed? Haha."

Perhaps it was a trick of the light, but I think I saw the slightest hint of a frown on the glasses-wearing Fixer.

"... Why don't you take some of our leftover ingredients with you? I'll give you a note with the mixing ratio on it, so try making some at home."

He handed us a meticulously packaged bag, complete with expertly prepared ingredients and detailed instructions on every step of the brewing process, from the mixing ratio and heat controls, all the way down to pouring it into a cup.
failureDesc:
We only looked away for a few seconds, but a few seconds was all it needed for an acrid smell of something burning to rise from the teapot.

"Ahh, you've got to reduce the heat!"

Despite our mad scramble to lower the heat, the Office was already filled with an unpleasant, burning stench.

"Eugh, I'm sick of this smell of ssanghwa— What the hell? Did something catch fire?"

A Fixer carrying a large trunk on her back walked into the Office and opened the windows to get the smell out.

"Ha ha ha. Why don't you all stop while you're ahead and let us treat you as guests?"

The old man gestured for us to sit, seemingly unconcerned about the mess we'd brought upon his office.
... Though we'll never know if he truly was unconcerned...

A little while later, a fresh cup of tea was set before us. The old man had brewed it himself.

dataList.title: The Knight of Despair
dataList.eventDesc: The knight extends a hand. Beneath the chill of her touch comes a wave of sorrow too great to bear.
dataList.behaveDesc: Which Sinner should receive the knight's blessing?
successDesc:
A wave of sorrow slowly washes over {0}.
A deep chill lingers where the knight's hand touched them.
Whether this will leave them with pride or despair remains to be seen.
failureDesc:
"If only... nothing had been left behind..."
A biting cold creeps across {0}'s skin.
Before long, it becomes a dark sorrow and engulfs their heart.
